_README: Colloquial -> statutory query expansion for the Assessing Department assistant.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Taxpayers do not use statutory vocabulary. Measured in the
sibling clerk project 2026-08-03: citizen phrasing pushed the governing statute
from rank 1 down to rank 10-19, so the model answered from secondary guidance or
honestly refused. The counter and the phone are exactly where plain language
arrives, so retrieval has to work in that register.
HOW IT WORKS. When a key phrase appears in the question, its statutory terms are
appended to the query token list before BM25 scoring. The taxpayer's own words are
always kept — expansion only ADDS signal, so a question already phrased
statutorily is unaffected.
MAINTENANCE. Add a key whenever staff notice a question the assistant handles
poorly in plain language but well in statutory language. Keys match as lowercase
substrings. Only use terms that genuinely appear in the corpus — expanding to
words the statutes never use adds noise, not recall.
GOTCHA (learned the hard way in the clerk project): keys must disambiguate INTENT.
A bare 'how long' appears in both 'how long to respond' and 'how long must you
keep', and expanding both ways poisoned one of them. Prefer longer, specific keys.

REGRESSION 2026-08-03: after the corpus grew to 243 documents, 'What is tax day in Michigan' pushed MCL 211.2 to rank 7 — one slot outside the window — because the newly-added millage-rollback bulletins outranked it, and the model then gave a WRONG definition of tax day from those. Statutory phrasing still ranked it 1st. Adding corpus can BREAK a previously-working question; re-measure after every expansion, and expect to add synonym keys as the corpus grows.
REGRESSION 2026-10-29 (brief 18b): the structured-chunking port split form-2602.md
(Request to Rescind Principal Residence Exemption) into small chunks, and the
W-A04 question ('moved out ... renting it to my nephew') no longer surfaced the
rescission form at all — the baseline run had correctly told the resident to file
Form 2602. There is no stemmer, so the resident's 'renting' never matched the
form's own 'rent part of your home / renters / rented' vocabulary. The 'renting'
and 'rent out' keys now carry those surface forms; measured effect: the
rescission chunk rises from rank ~7 (unserved) to the served set, and BM25 gives
zero delta to every chunk that was outranking it.
REGRESSION 2026-10-29 #2 (brief 18b gate): the same port scattered MCL 211.24c
(annual notice of assessment) into 16 subsection chunks, and for 'What must the
annual notice of assessment change tell the owner, and when must it be sent?'
NOT ONE of them served — the question's words are exactly the words every STC
bulletin and manual section also uses, so the statute's chunks ranked as low as
168th. The statute's own subsection labels carry the token '24c', which the
question never says; the 'notice of assessment' key now adds it. Measured
effect: 211.24c(4) (14-day mailing deadline) serves at rank 2 and 211.24c(1)
(notice contents) at rank 6; A/B over all 48 eval cases: 1/48 served sets
change (the target case only).
